stemBlocks.value: The voltage across a resistor is given by V = IR, where I is the current and R is the resistance. Make R the subject of the formula, then find R when V = 24 V and I = 3.
Think first: This is a one-step rearrangement followed by a one-step substitution.

stemBlocks.altText: Source visual for edmar-csec-p056-q16 from workbook page 56.

strategyBlocks.value: Divide both sides by I to make R the subject, then substitute V = 24 and I = 3.

finalAnswerBlocks.value: R = V/I, and when V = 24 V and I = 3, R = 8 ohms

whyThisWorks.value: Because V, I and R are linked by a single product, any one of them can be found from the other two by dividing or multiplying. Rearranging first means you can reuse R = V/I for any pair of values without redoing the algebra each time.

commonErrors.misconception: Writing R = IV instead of V/I.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Writing R = IV instead of V/I.

commonErrors.misconception: Dividing the current by the voltage, giving 3/24 = 0.125.
commonErrors.correctiveNote: Avoid this: Dividing the current by the voltage, giving 3/24 = 0.125.

examTip.value: State the rearranged formula on its own line before substituting - examiners award a mark for the correct transposition.
